title: Isolated/VPC incremental-upgrade contract and minimal-egress operator requirements
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Product requirements and acceptance criteria for performing incremental OS/container/operator upgrades in fully isolated VPC/private deployments. Focus: minimal egress allowlist, deterministic offline image staging, signed artifact verification, staged canary sequencing, and safe rollback behaviors when no external network is available.
requirements: Operator must support an 'islanded' upgrade mode that consumes artifacts from a configurable local mirror or mounted storage without outbound network calls.
Provide a compact egress allowlist.json template: up to 12 FQDNs + 6 ports and an explicit CIDR for mirror endpoints. Customers may supply mirror IPs instead of hostnames.
Image and manifest signing: all images and manifests consumed by the operator must be signed. Operator verifies signatures using customer-provided public keys stored in KMS or a provided PEM file.

Upgrade sequencing: support multi-phase canary where 5% of nodes are upgraded from mirror artifacts, health-checked for at least 10 minutes, then 25%, then 100%. Each phase must be abortable with automatic rollback to prior image.
Deterministic offline verification: operator must compute and compare SHA256 checksums of staged blobs before applying. Checksums surfaced in UI and runbook logs.
KMS/HSM rotation: allow rotation of signing verification keys without requiring outbound connectivity; provide operator tool to import rotated keys via mirror or bundle file.

Telemetry and health: operator emits a minimal 'heartbeat' stub to local telemetry collector; telemetry payloads must support redaction and be configurable to zero-out customer data when exported to hosted plane.
Fallback proxies: if a limited egress window is configured, operator must support staged artifact fetch with retry-backoff and circuit-breaker to avoid extended egress bursts.
Offline rollback: support atomic rollback that restores node-local state and local operator-managed caches within a 60 minute SLO for a failed canary phase.
Operator CLI: include 'verify-mirror' and 'dry-run-upgrade' commands that validate artifact set, signatures, checksums, and minimal network rules prior to live upgrade.
Documentation: step-by-step offline upgrade playbook for SREs plus a condensed checklist for customer operators. Include sample iptables and split-horizon DNS rules for mirror usage.
acceptance_criteria: Offline canary validation: Teams can perform a full canary using only a staged mirror (no external internet) and the upgrade completes to 5% nodes with successful health checks within configured thresholds.
Signature enforcement: Operator rejects any artifact whose signature validation fails. Test artifact with mismatched signature returns clear operator error and no partial apply.
Checksum verification: Staged artifacts are checksummed and verified by operator before any container is swapped. Tests include both valid and tampered blobs.
KMS rotation without egress: Key rotation can be executed by importing a key bundle via mirror and the operator continues to validate previously signed artifacts after rotation.
Rollback reliability: Injected failure during 25% canary causes automatic rollback within 30 minutes and all nodes return to previous healthy state with no data loss in operator-managed metadata.

Minimal telemetry: When 'hosted-telemetry=false', no outbound telemetry leaves the VPC. 'Heartbeat-only' mode must still allow on-prem observability (local Prometheus scrape) without hosted plane egress.
Egress window simulation: Simulated 10-minute egress windows can successfully pull required artifacts without operator-induced egress spikes outside the window.
Runbook automation: Playbook 'offline-upgrade.md' referenced in the ticket reproduces the upgrade steps end-to-end and is validated by Solutions Engineering during acceptance testing.

Operational metrics: New metrics exposed in Console: offline_upgrade_phase, offline_checksum_failures, offline_signature_failures, offline_rollback_count; each emits at least one sample during tests and appears in dashboards.
Security review sign-off: Security team provides written approval of the offline key import flow and the redaction rules for telemetry prior to release.
scope_changes: Initial PRD included full remote bootstrap via hosted control plane; scope narrowed to require an explicit customer-provided mirror or bundle for offline installs.
Removed support for physical media distribution automation (e.g., tape/USB shipping) from MVP — will be scoped as a separate follow-up with Operations.
Expanded CLI surface to include 'verify-mirror' and 'dry-run-upgrade' after early engineering feedback to improve preflight confidence.
Added requirement to surface checksums in Console runbook view after customer pilot feedback requesting artifact visibility.
Deferred automatic split-horizon DNS provisioning; provide configuration templates instead.
risks: Customer misconfiguration of mirror IPs or DNS leads to silent upgrade failures — mitigated by operator preflight and clearer error messages.
KMS integration edge cases where keys are rotated but bundles are not applied resulting in signature verification storms during upgrades.
Telemetry redaction bugs could accidentally export sensitive strings to hosted plane unless redaction is enforced and E2E-tested.
Rollback may not be instantaneous on very large clusters due to local filesystem persistence ordering; SREs must validate performance on >100 node clusters.
Customer expectation mismatch: customers expect offline upgrades to be zero-touch; communicate explicitly that operator requires a staged mirror or import bundle.
notes: Design and engineering should prototype the 'verify-mirror' flow and produce a demo that runs entirely from a local HTTP mirror. Coordinate with Security for a tabletop exercise simulating a compromised mirror artifact. Notify Solutions Engineering to schedule two customer pilots (one VPC, one air-gapped) in December.
